subject: Lighthouse Labs — renewal + capacity increase: rate smoothing & growth credits
messages:
From: Aaron Mills <aaron@lighthouse.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lighthouse.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity bump — Q3 go-live target

Diego,

Quick summary: Lighthouse Labs is planning to renew for another 12 months but we need to double our committed capacity starting July 1 to support a new product line. Budget is constrained — we can’t absorb a straight price-per-token increase. Looking for options that:
- smooth pricing over the next 12 months (no step increases mid-year)
- include credits to offset migration/engineering costs
- allow burst capacity to be billed against credits when needed

I attached our draft SOW for the incremental workload (Lighthouse_SOW_Q2_2027.pdf). Can your team put forward a concrete proposal — pricing, credit structure, and any contractual language we should expect? Procurement is looped in.

Target timeline: proposal this week, DocuSign-ready term sheet by the end of next week so we can hit a July 1 start.

Thanks — Aaron
Aaron Mills
Head of Platform & Ops
Lighthouse Labs
aaron@lighthouse.ai
+1 415-555-0134

Attachment: Lighthouse_SOW_Q2_2027.pdf (pdf, 240KB)
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Mills <aaron@lighthouse.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity bump — Q3 go-live target

Aaron — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. We can absolutely put together a couple of pragmatic paths that balance your budget constraint with predictable unit economics. High level options we’ll propose:

Option A — 12-month, moderate uplift
- 2x committed capacity starting 2027-07-01
- blended unit price with an 18% effective discount vs current list
- $75k onboarding/migration credit applied over first 90 days (usable for burst)
- 60-day price smoothing guarantee (no per-token increases during first 60 days)

Option B — 24-month, price-hold + growth credit
- longer-term commit with a price hold for 12 months
- larger upfront credit ($150k) that vests as usage grows (credits usable for burst and preemptible capacity)
- quarterly review + optional capacity top-up window with pre-negotiated uplift rates

Next steps: I’ll loop Ben to finalize numbers and include a spreadsheet proposal. Vanessa will outline onboarding timeline and success milestones. If that looks like a fit, we’ll route to Laura for contract redline prep. Can we pencil in a 30-minute call Monday to walk through Option A vs B?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal + capacity bump — Q3 go-live target

Aaron / team — attaching a numbers workbook (redwood_proposal_LH-2027-021.xlsx) with concrete pricing cells and examples of monthly cashflow under both options. Key commercial highlights:

- Blended unit price (Option A): $0.0056 per token-equivalent (18% discount vs list), $75k one-time credit applied evenly over the first three invoices; credits can be invoked to offset burst overage.
- Blended unit price (Option B): $0.0049 per token-equivalent for a 24-month term; $150k credit that vests at 25% increments once usage exceeds committed baseline.
- PO + billing: Procurement will need a Purchase Order referencing deal LH-2027-021; payments net 30 unless you request net 45 and we can include that in the spreadsheet as a sensitivity.
- Finance note: credits are applied as invoice line item discounts (not refunds) and expire if not used within 12 months.

I’ve included a sample amortization schedule and an example showing how credits cover burst charges during the first 90 days. If procurement needs a split-invoice approach (upfront + monthly), we can model that as well.

Laura — tagging you for a quick redline once Lighthouse confirms a direction. Vanessa — can you sketch a 6-week onboarding timeline that aligns to a July 1 start if Lighthouse signs by 05/14?

Happy to join the Monday call.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Sales
redwood@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_proposal_LH-2027-021.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)
From: Aaron Mills <aaron@lighthouse.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lighthouse.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity bump — Q3 go-live target

Thanks Ben / Diego — useful detail. A few clarifications from procurement and product:

1) Commit flexibility: we can’t fully double the baseline commitment right away. Can we start at +50% committed, with an agreed cadence to scale to 2x by Q4? If credits apply during the ramp that helps.
2) Credit usability: the credit must be usable for burst and for paid support hours associated with migration (we have a small engineering window to cover).
3) Price-lock window: procurement needs a 90-day price lock after signing (not just 60 days) to finalize their internal budgeting.

If you can update the workbook with a staged-commit ramp (50% -> 75% -> 100% -> 200% by Oct 1) and show how credits are consumed against burst and support hours, we’ll review with finance. Also please prepare a DocuSign-ready term sheet — we can get approval fast if the economics are right.

Thanks — Aaron
Aaron Mills
Head of Platform & Ops
Lighthouse Labs

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Mills <aaron@lighthouse.ai>, procurement@lighthouse.ai
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Updated proposal + redline (next steps)

Aaron — appreciate the clarity. Attached are: (1) an updated pricing workbook that models the staged ramp you requested, (2) a contract redline (contract_redline_v1.docx) that reflects: the 90-day price-lock, credit usage for burst and professional services, and a limited vesting schedule for the larger credit under Option B.

Quick summary of changes implemented:
- Staged commit ramp: +50% on 2027-07-01, +75% on 2027-08-01, +100% on 2027-09-01, 2x baseline by 2027-10-01. Monthly example cashflows included.
- Credits: $75k onboarding credit (Option A) restructured so 40% covers professional services (migration + support hours) and 60% is available for burst consumption; credits apply to invoice line items and expire 12 months after signing.
- Price lock: 90 days from effective date (applies to per-token rates only; other operational fees subject to normal adjustments with 30-day notice).
- Contract: Laura’s redline narrows the indemnity scope around third-party model usage and requires a mutual audit-rights clause; we kept the commercial terms standard for speed to signature.

Next actions (ask list):
- Aaron / procurement: confirm the staged ramp cadence and whether you want the Option A (shorter term) or Option B (longer-term price hold + larger credit).
- Procurement: please provide PO number and billing cadence preference (monthly vs. split upfront + monthly).
- Vanessa: I’ve asked her to include a 6-week onboarding plan keyed to the ramp milestones. Vanessa — can you confirm required prework and an initial kickoff date?
- Laura Bennet (Legal): please review final redline and flag any high-risk clauses.

For convenience I’ve also linked the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345) and a working Google doc for the term sheet: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcdFakeProposal. If everything looks good, we’ll convert to DocuSign-ready copy and route.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Attachment: contract_redline_v1.docx (docx, 35KB)
